title: As they expand in China, Europe’s companies are hollowing out Europe
gist: MERICS comment by Andreas Mischer arguing that European (especially German) companies' deepening 'localization' in China is hollowing out Europe's industrial base: VW, Mercedes and BMW saw >30% China sales slumps in Q2 2026 yet keep localizing, BASF opened an EUR 8.7bn Zhanjiang site while cutting jobs at home, and suppliers like Bosch and ZF cut German jobs while expanding in China. He urges mandatory EU outbound-investment screening and conditioning EU funds on retaining R&D and industrial capacity in Europe.

insights.claim: Andreas Mischer argues that European companies' drive to localize value chains in China threatens EU 'derisking' and comes at the expense of the EU's industrial competitiveness.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Policy backlash against China localization is building; watch EU outbound-investment rules.
insights.quote: these advantages come at the expense of the EU’s industrial competitiveness
insights.locator: European companies are moving ever more

insights.claim: Historically companies built factories abroad to exploit scale and reinvest profits at home in R&D and high-value jobs, but European companies in China now reinvest locally while cutting jobs at home, putting boardroom decisions in conflict with Europe's long-term economic interests.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Breakdown of the 'profits home' model weakens the political case for China exposure; regulatory risk for China-heavy European firms.
insights.quote: European companies that built factories in China are locally reinvesting the profit they make there while cutting jobs at home

themes.theme: German autos: losing battle despite 'in China, for China'

insights.claim: Volkswagen built its largest R&D center outside Germany in Hefei and, with partner Xpeng, aims to cut its China R&D costs by up to 50% via fewer electronic control units and earlier supplier involvement.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Shows depth of VW's China-for-China pivot and reliance on Chinese partners for tech.
insights.quote: reduce Volkswagen’s R&D costs in China by up to 50 percent

insights.claim: In Q2 2026, Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz and BMW each saw China sales slump by more than 30% year-on-year, despite aggressive localization.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: German OEM China profit pools are collapsing; bearish signal for their China earnings.
insights.quote: Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz, and BMW each saw sales slump by more than 30 percent year-on-year
insights.locator: German carmakers seem to be fighting

insights.claim: Volkswagen closed its Nanjing factory in 2025 after 17 years with SAIC, and VW-SAIC factory utilization that year was estimated at just 58% of 2.1 million cars annual capacity.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Idle capacity creates pressure for write-downs or repurposing toward export.
insights.quote: Estimates put utilization across all VW-SAIC’s factories that year at just 58 percent of a total annual capacity of 2.1 million cars
insights.locator: German carmakers seem to be fighting

insights.claim: With idle Chinese capacity and China's 15th Five-Year Plan for intelligent and connected vehicles urging joint ventures to focus on exports, European carmakers may shift to export-oriented localization, adding Chinese-made cars to the flood into Europe and compounding their home-market problems.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Watch JV export volumes to Europe; could intensify EU tariff/trade-defense measures and pressure European auto margins.
insights.quote: adding to the flood of Chinese-made cars into Europe – and compounding their own problems in their home market
insights.locator: With so much capacity sitting idle

themes.theme: BASF Zhanjiang bet and its risks

insights.claim: BASF inaugurated its EUR 8.7 billion integrated chemical plant in Zhanjiang in March 2026, the largest single investment in company history, while cutting 2,800 jobs at its Ludwigshafen headquarters since 2024.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Capital is visibly migrating from European to Chinese chemicals capacity.

insights.claim: BASF expects Zhanjiang to generate EUR 5 billion in sales by 2030 and lift China to 20% of its revenue; China accounts for half of global chemicals demand but only 14% of BASF sales.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: BASF's China growth case hinges on Zhanjiang ramp; key KPI to track.
insights.quote: The country accounts for half of global chemicals demand but makes up only 14 percent of BASF’s sales.

insights.claim: BASF concedes Zhanjiang will become profitable later than planned because China's chemicals sector is beset by overcapacity and low margins; the company bets Beijing can stamp out 'involution,' but timing is uncertain.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Delayed returns; anti-involution policy success is the swing factor for China chemicals margins.
insights.quote: the Zhanjiang site will become profitable later than originally planned

insights.claim: China's recently revised national defense mobilization law allows the government to seize company assets in certain circumstances, a tail risk foreign investors should now factor in given geopolitical uncertainty.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Expropriation tail risk for foreign fixed assets in China; relevant to valuation discounts.
insights.quote: allows the government to seize company assets in certain circumstances

themes.theme: Suppliers: cutting at home, expanding in China

insights.claim: Virtually all major German car-parts suppliers are cutting jobs at home while expanding in China: Bosch plans 22,000 global job cuts by 2030, many in Germany, and ZF Friedrichshafen 14,000 in Germany alone.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: German industrial employment erosion feeds political pressure for industrial policy and protectionism.
insights.locator: A third group of German companies

insights.claim: Volkswagen's plan to cut another 50,000 jobs and close up to four factories is the most prominent example of the hollowing out of European industrial capacity and growing deindustrialization threat.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Deindustrialization is a structural theme for German macro and politics.
insights.quote: the most prominent example of hollowing out of European industrial capacity
insights.locator: A third group of German companies

insights.claim: Mischer recommends EU leaders make outbound-investment screening mandatory and expand it beyond semiconductors, AI and quantum (the 2025 Commission monitoring request) to more technologies and sectors.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Possible EU outbound-investment regime would constrain European corporate China capex; watch Council proposals.
insights.quote: EU leaders should now make screenings mandatory and expand this regime to more technologies and sectors
insights.locator: The EU should do more than protect

insights.claim: Mischer proposes making access to EU public funds conditional on companies retaining R&D and industrial capacity within Europe.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Conditionality on subsidies could reshape European firms' capex geography.
insights.quote: making access to EU public funds conditional on retaining R&D and industrial capacity within Europe
insights.locator: The EU should do more than protect
